text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Kuwait hands humanitarian aid to Iraqi refugees stranded in the Iraq-Iran border area.
- Parliamentarian Hassan Jawhar says reconciliation with countries which sided with Iraq during its 1990-91 occupation is purely a governmental desire.

- MP Adnan Abdul-Samad says the government should reconsider a deal to buy British missiles. The government has told parliament it had approved a recommendation by a specialised committee to buy British Aerospace Plc Sea Skua missiles dropping what MPs described as a cheaper offer to buy missiles from France's Aerospatiale.
- Health official says Kuwait will not grant residency permits to foreigners who prove to be HIV positive.
- Medical sources in Vienna say Iraq's vice-chairman of the Revolutionary Command Council Izzat Ibarhim is suffering leukaemia.
- Oil Minister Isa al-Mazeedi leaves for Tunisia on Wednesday on official visit.
- Leading Kuwaiti economist Jassem al-Saadoun says market prices of some shares listed on the Kuwait Stock Exchange are exaggerated.
- Police arrest three Filipinos for trafficking narcotics.
